sections.vendors: H&M Group signed a multi-year supply agreement with Recover (RCotton) for recycled cotton fibre sourced from post-industrial textile waste. The brand also deepened its Circulose partnership for MMCF (man-made cellulosic fibre) made from recycled cotton blends. Both partnerships signal a shift from virgin cotton towards closed-loop fibre supply.
sections.sustainability: H&M Group reported 91% of materials sourced through more sustainable routes, tracking towards its 2030 100% target. The group continues to push supplier compliance on Higg MSI scores and has introduced new minimum thresholds for chemical management under its ZDHC commitment.
sections.sourcing: H&M is consolidating its supplier base to work with fewer, larger strategic partners amid geopolitical disruptions. The group is accelerating nearshoring to Turkey and reshoring of some European production for speed-sensitive fast-fashion lines, while retaining Bangladesh and India for volume basics.
sections.strategy: H&M Group streamlined its corporate structure in 2026, reducing management layers to improve speed-to-market. The group is doubling down on full-price sell-through rates after years of margin pressure from markdown dependency, targeting improved inventory management and tighter open-to-buy discipline.
sections.pricing: H&M raised prices modestly on sustainable material lines to partially offset the green premium on certified fibres. The group is testing value-anchored pricing architecture to protect its mid-market position against Shein and Primark at the bottom.
sections.launches: H&M launched a new Conscious Exclusive capsule using Circulose and recycled cashmere for AW2026. The group's & Other Stories and COS brands introduced elevated sustainable ranges targeting premium segments.
sections.gossip: Industry sources suggest H&M Group is under continued pressure from activist shareholders to accelerate climate commitments. Some analysts flagged that 91% sustainable materials still includes BCI cotton, which carries weaker guarantees than GOTS or organic certification.
soWhat: Recover/RCotton multi-year deal signals growing H&M demand for recycled cotton — suppliers in Bangladesh and India with recycled blended fabric capability should pitch certified GRS recycled cotton constructions
Supplier base consolidation means fewer new vendors will gain entry — existing H&M approved suppliers need to invest in certifications and scale to stay on the list
Nearshoring to Turkey for speed-to-market lines creates opportunity for Turkish fabric mills to pitch faster replenishment programmes with shorter lead times
